speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with a generalized rash. To help me understand what you are experiencing, how many days old are you?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the information. Since the rash started on day of life 3 in a term infant whose mother has a history of gonorrhea, does the rash include any pustules or crusted lesions, particularly around the eyes or mouth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Gonococcal Infection (Disseminated Gonococcal Infection). The clinical presentation of a pustular rash with an erythematous base sparing the palms and soles in a 4-day-old infant born to a mother with a history of gonorrhea is pathognomonic. I request Gram stain and culture of skin lesions to confirm the diagnosis.
